answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a yarrow as the anchor of the cost.
